item.title: Indiana State Police arrest 2 for street racing near Bloomington
item.description: Indiana State Police arrested two people for street racing on State Road 37 near Bloomington after they were caught going 102 and 104 miles per hour.

item.title: Indianapolis man arrested after fleeing police on I-69 in northern Indiana
item.description: Adolfo Mejia-Fuentes, 19, of Indianapolis, was arrested after a high-speed chase on I-69 in northern Indiana, state police say. Officers deployed tire deflation devices and engaged in a brief foot chase.

item.title: Shipshewana town marshal arrested on intimidation charges
item.description: Juan Carlos Jasso, 49-year-old Town Marshall of Shipshewana, Indiana, turned himself in Monday after a warrant was issued for alleged intimidation, following a months-long investigation into a domestic battery incident.

item.title: Indiana lawmakers consider changes to utility bill calculations
item.description: House Republicans are pushing a measure to enact performance-based ratemaking in Indiana, which would require utilities to meet certain targets for affordability and reliability before regulators approve any rate increases, and would also require budget billing for all residential customers.

item.title: Girl Scouts of Central Indiana appoints Deana Potterf as CEO
item.description: Deana Potterf has been appointed as the new CEO of the Girl Scouts of Central Indiana, bringing nearly three decades of service to the organization.

item.title: Butler University to launch degree in deaf education in fall
item.description: Butler University has received a $1.25 million grant to launch a new Master of Arts in Deaf Education program in fall 2026, which will prepare educators to work with children who are deaf or hard of hearing using listening and spoken language approaches.

item.title: Lawmakers advance legislation to dissolve hundreds of Indiana townships
item.description: A bill advanced from a House panel would dissolve all Indiana townships with a population of less than 6,700 or if at least 80% of their land area is located within the boundaries of a municipality. The measure, now on its way to the full House, could affect up to 700 of the state's 1,000 townships.

item.title: Assembly Hall to host free watch party for CFP National Championship
item.description: IU Athletics is hosting a watch party at Simon Skjodt Assembly Hall for the Hoosiers' College Football Playoff National Championship game against the Miami Hurricanes, with doors opening at 6 p.m. Monday. Free digital tickets were available online on Tuesday night.
